brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4445 The Cornice Baker: a baker on the garden level bakes the block's brownstone details in miniature, edible cornices and brackets and stoop balusters in gingerbread and burnt sugar, and once a year the buildings taste themselves, the block dining on its own architecture at one long table, each house saving its cast iron railing candy for last, eye flowers opening in the spun sugar, color story: burnt sugar amber and gingerbread umber over ink black.

name: The Dumbwaiter Postal Service
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4446 The Dumbwaiter Postal Service: the dumbwaiters of a brownstone row never stopped running, threading the party walls in secret, and the children of the block operate them as a postal service between houses, contracts in crayon, packages of cookies and marbles and one guinea pig in transit at all hours, the adults pretending not to know, eye flowers opening in the shaft ropes, color story: dumbwaiter rope hemp and crayon spectrum over ink black.

name: The Garden Level Root Cellar of Dreams
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4447 The Garden Level Root Cellar of Dreams: under a Fort Greene brownstone the old root cellar stores the household's dreams in mason jars, generations deep, and tonight a granddaughter down for preserves takes a nineteen fifty two jar by mistake, uncorking her grandmother's dream of dancing at the Savoy, the cellar filling with big band and the smell of gardenias, eye flowers opening between the jars, color story: mason jar green and savoy brass over ink black.

name: The Newel Post Guardian
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4448 The Newel Post Guardian: the carved walnut newel post of a Harlem brownstone holds the house's spirit in its globe finial, polished by a century of palms, and when the house sells at auction the finial goes dark until the new owner, a night shift paramedic, wraps her hand around it after her first bad call, the globe kindling for her like a struck match, eye flowers opening in the walnut grain, color story: walnut oil brown and finial kindle gold over ink black.

name: The Skylight Well Choir
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4449 The Skylight Well Choir: the stacked stairwells of a brownstone row share one acoustic soul, and on Sunday evenings the residents sing up their skylight wells, five houses of separate voices meeting above the roofs in one braided chord audible only to the pigeons and one astonished drone pilot, eye flowers opening in the skylight glass, color story: skylight dusk lilac and stairwell runner burgundy over ink black.

name: The Boiler Room Dragon
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4450 The Boiler Room Dragon: the octopus furnace in a brownstone cellar is a small ancient dragon in an iron shell, ducts for arms, fed coal ceremonially by the house's ten year old on cold mornings, a partnership of solemn nods, the radiators upstairs purring, the dragon's one visible eye glowing behind the fire door with something like love, eye flowers opening in the duct joints, color story: fire door orange and cellar shadow slate over ink black.

name: The Party Wall Piano
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4451 The Party Wall Piano: two pianists in adjoining brownstones have played duets through their shared wall for thirty years without meeting, the wall thinning to velvet where the music passes, and tonight, both widowed now, they each lay a hand flat on the plaster mid nocturne and feel the other's warmth for the first time, eye flowers opening along the party wall, color story: piano rosewood and plaster warm white over ink black.

name: The Areaway Lighthouse
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4452 The Areaway Lighthouse: the below stairs areaway of a corner brownstone keeps a small lighthouse, a gas lamp the house refuses to let die, and it guides the block's night wanderers home, drunks and insomniacs and one runaway who follows the green brass glow to the garden door where soup is always somehow just made, eye flowers opening in the lamp glass, color story: gas lamp green and areaway iron black over ink black.

name: The Lintel Inscription
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4453 The Lintel Inscription: the brownstone lintels of one Crown Heights block carry invisible inscriptions readable only by touch, each doorway naming what the house most needs, and a blind locksmith walks the block on Sundays reading the stones with his fingers, leaving the right small repairs like offerings, a tightened hinge, an oiled lock, a long overdue knock, eye flowers opening under his fingertips, color story: lintel sandstone and locksmith brass over ink black.

name: The Ivy Correspondence
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4454 The Ivy Correspondence: the ivy on two facing brownstones grows in matched patterns, a slow green correspondence across the street conducted over decades, and the botanist who finally decodes it finds a love letter still being written, the houses having watched their original owners part on that sidewalk in nineteen twelve, finishing the couple's sentence for them, eye flowers opening in the ivy script, color story: ivy green and letter shadow claret over ink black.

name: The Attic Wind Archive
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4455 The Attic Wind Archive: the top floor of a Park Slope brownstone archives every gust that ever rattled its windows, wind kept in labeled hatboxes, and on airless August nights the family opens a box of March nineteen fifty eight on the landing, the stairwell filling with cold that smells of coal smoke and wet wool, the children riding the banister through it, eye flowers opening among the hatboxes, color story: hatbox stripe teal and archived wind silver over ink black.

name: The Mantel of Small Gods
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4456 The Mantel of Small Gods: a brownstone parlor mantel has accreted a century of left objects into a shrine of small gods, subway token and baby shoe and harmonica and one chess knight, each humming faintly, and the new tenants learn the house rule from a note in the flue, add one thing you love, take nothing, dust gently, eye flowers opening among the objects, color story: mantel marble white and small god patina bronze over ink black.

name: The Stoop Wedding
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4457 The Stoop Wedding: a couple who met on this stoop marries on it, guests banked up both neighboring stoops like bleachers, and at the vows every brownstone on the block turns on its parlor chandeliers at once, twenty warm windows rising behind the couple like the city's own candles, the buildings' gift, unasked, eye flowers opening down the balustrade, color story: chandelier gold and wedding dusk periwinkle over ink black.

name: The Basement Recording Studio of 1974
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4458 The Basement Recording Studio of 1974: a brownstone basement still holds the reel to reel studio where one perfect record was cut in nineteen seventy four, and on humid nights the session resumes, bass through the floorboards, and the drummer's granddaughter, who lives upstairs now, finally takes her keyboard down to sit in with the ghosts, who make room without stopping, eye flowers opening in the acoustic foam, color story: reel tape brown and studio lamp red over ink black.

name: The Roof Ridge Regatta
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4459 The Roof Ridge Regatta: on the first warm Sunday the brownstone roofs of one long block unmoor and sail, cornices for prows, whole rooflines tacking gently against the sky while remaining somehow attached, families picnicking on the pitched slopes as their houses race at the speed of drifting clouds, the block championship decided by inches over six hours, eye flowers opening at the ridge lines, color story: roof slate blue and picnic blanket cherry over ink black.

name: The Hall Mirror's Long Memory
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4460 The Hall Mirror's Long Memory: the pier mirror in a brownstone hall shows each person leaving the house at the age they were happiest in it, and the family has stopped explaining this to guests, tonight a grown son home for the funeral catching his reflection at nine years old in a cowboy hat, his mother visible behind him in the glass, waving from nineteen ninety one, eye flowers opening in the gilt frame, color story: mirror silver and cowboy hat tan over ink black.

name: The Brownstone Midwife
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4461 The Brownstone Midwife: when a house on the block is gut renovated, one retired midwife sits with it through the demolition nights, hand on the party wall, talking it through the loss of its plaster the way she talked mothers through labor, and the block swears the renovated houses she attends keep their souls, the ones she misses come back hollow, eye flowers opening in the exposed lath, color story: lath pale straw and midwife shawl deep teal over ink black.

name: The Fire Escape Conservatory
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4462 The Fire Escape Conservatory: a horn player who lost his apartment but not his block lives across four fire escapes with the buildings' consent, bed on one landing, kitchen on another, practicing at golden hour suspended over the street, and the four families whose windows he passes set extra places at four different tables, his address given as the air between houses, eye flowers opening along the iron landings, color story: horn brass and golden hour apricot over ink black.

name: The Widow's Walk Semaphore
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4463 The Widow's Walk Semaphore: two great grandmothers on facing widow's walks have signaled each other nightly for sixty years with kerosene lanterns, a private code of swings and pauses, and tonight the block below finally learns what the lights have been saying all along, a running count of every good thing that happened on the street that day, sixty years, never once zero, eye flowers opening in the lantern arcs, color story: kerosene flame gold and widow walk rail black over ink black.

name: The House That Grew a Room
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4464 The House That Grew a Room: the night the fourth child is born the brownstone grows a room for her, pushing out a bay that wasn't there at sunset, plaster rose on the new ceiling, the neighbors bringing housewarming gifts for the room itself, and the buildings department inspector closing his folder and writing, after a long pause, preexisting condition, eye flowers opening in the new plaster rose, color story: new plaster blush and inspector folder manila over ink black.

name: The Block Association of Souls
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4465 The Block Association of Souls: the annual block association meeting seats the houses themselves, each brownstone attending as a grave brown clad elder with a stoop straight back, sitting among their tenants in the community room, voting on tree pits and speed bumps, and the humans have long stopped finding it strange that the motion always carries when the houses rise together, eye flowers opening in their brownstone lapels, color story: brownstone elder umber and community room fluorescent mint over ink black.

name: The Last Light on the Parlor Floor
brief: NEW YORKERS by MLow, character 4466 The Last Light on the Parlor Floor: every night at eleven one parlor window on the block is granted the last light, the house chosen by need, and tonight it is the young teacher grading at her table who looks up to find her ordinary lamp burning like a hearth of honey, the whole block's warmth routed through one bulb, her radiator knocking twice, which means, from a building, courage, eye flowers opening in the lamplight, color story: last light honey and parlor shadow mulberry over ink black.
